newsitem.title: SPAIN: Three jailed ETA rebels condemn killing in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Three jailed ETA rebels condemn killing in Spain.

text.p: Three jailed ETA guerrillas on Thursday condemned the killing of a young politician by their fellow Basque rebels, signalling growing divisions within the radical separatist movement.

Adding their voices to the national outcry against the murder of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, the three men, reading a statement to reporters at a Basque prison, said ETA in recent days has "managed to accumulate more hate than in 38 years of terrorism."

The prisoners, Jose Manuel Soares Gamboa, Luis Gaston and Luis Gorriti, also denounced ETA's political arm Herri Batasuna, which has been accused by mainstream Spanish leaders of acting as "accomplices" to Blanco's killing.

Reading the statement to reporters, Soares Gamboa -- implicated in numerous ETA killings while a member of the group's Madrid cell in the 1980s -- said: "I condemn you, ETA. I condemn you, Herri Batasuna. I condemn your crimes and tortures."
"I affirm that one vote for Herri Batasuna is a bullet linked to ETA," he said.

It was the strongest sign yet of an emerging rift within the ranks of the ETA movement after Blanco's killing last weekend sparked national outrage. Millions of Spaniards have taken to the streets to vent their anger.
Soares Gamboa said Herri Batasuna's lawyers had threatened him and "asked whether I've gone crazy because saying what I'm saying could cost me dearly.
"Perhaps I am crazy, but the the last one to abandon ETA will be an idiot," he said.
When ETA rebels kidnapped the Basque town councillor on July 10, they justified it as an action taken to help rebel comrades dispersed in jails throughout Spain.

The guerrillas demanded that 500 inmates be transferred to prisons in the autonomous Basque region within 48 hours. The government refused, and Blanco was shot in the head on Saturday. He died 12 hours later.
